title: Refactor focus order and ARIA semantics for nested table controls; produce VPAT artifacts
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: A recent accessibility audit flagged inconsistent focus order and missing ARIA semantics in nested table rows that contain interactive controls (expand/collapse, inline actions, sort buttons). Chart legend items are not keyboard-focusable and our color tokens don't provide clear high-contrast fallbacks for compact-density tables. We must refactor the focus model, update ARIA attributes, and ship a small VPAT artifact set that demonstrates conformance for the affected components.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level: All interactive elements inside table rows (buttons, links, menu toggles) follow a deterministic DOM and tabindex order matching visual flow across compact and regular density variants.
Column headers with sort or filter controls expose correct ARIA semantics (aria-sort, aria-haspopup) and have unique aria-labels/aria-describedby references.
Expand/collapse row controls move focus predictably (focus moves to first actionable control inside expanded row); no keyboard traps exist.
Chart legends are reachable via keyboard, have clear focus styling, and update an aria-live polite region when toggled to announce state changes for screen reader users.
Contrast tokens: introduce high-contrast token set for compact tables and chart legends; automated CSS variables documentation and Figma token update complete.
VPAT artifacts: draft VPAT snippets and test evidence (axeCore runs + manual SR checks) for the affected components included in the design-system accessibility folder.
QA: Regression tests added to component stories demonstrating keyboard-only navigation and screen reader output transcripts.
Documentation: update component docs with keyboard interaction patterns, recommended ARIA usage, and examples for custom integrations.
design_notes: Proposed approach: centralize focus handling for data-row variant using a FocusZone-ish pattern with skip logic for purely decorative cells.
Replace ad-hoc tabindex management with documented focus-order rules: 1) row-expander 2) primary action 3) secondary actions 4) row contextual menu.
Create a compact/high-contrast palette token (token name: --rwd-color-contrast-compact-1) with WCAG AA/AAA mappings and add to token migration spreadsheet.
Chart legend: design compact focus ring and hover state; show visual and invisible label pairing for screen reader (aria-labelledby referencing legend text).
Provide Figma interactive prototype for keyboard walkthroughs (link in links).
engineering_notes: ENG needs: helper utilities for aria-describedby glue (generate stable IDs), focus management hook, and an opt-in aria-live region per chart instance.
Avoid virtualizing focus by DOM reorder; instead maintain DOM order but hide/show content to preserve reading order and focus predictability.
Backend: no data-model change; front-end only. Ensure automated visual-diff tests don't flag acceptable focus-ring color changes (update baseline where appropriate).
Performance: focus utilities should be lightweight; follow existing design-system patterns used in dropdown and modal components.
qa_plan: Manual test matrix: VoiceOver (macOS), NVDA + Firefox (Windows), TalkBack (Android) — keyboard-only and screen reader flows for sample datasets (dense table with 100 rows; nested row with 4 interactive controls).
Automated: axeCore CI scan on component stories; add jest-dom ARIA checks for aria-sort and aria-haspopup where applicable.
Record SR transcripts for the chart legend toggles and include them in the VPAT evidence zip.
Cross-browser check: focus rings look and meet contrast on latest Chrome, Safari, Firefox on Mac and Windows.
